# Antagonist Rules Antagonists are given the responsibility of moving the round’s story forward in a way that is interesting and engaging to all involved parties. While antagonists are given many special privileges when compared to crew-aligned characters, there are still rules and precedents you are required to follow.
Antagonism and its limits can be complex and nuanced. If you are ever unsure about the limits of your specific type of antagonist, you should always ask in admin help (F1) [bold]before[/bold] you act on your plan.
If you are assigned an antagonist role at any point, you are [bold]required[/bold] to drive the round forward in an antagonistic way. You should not wait until the evacuation shuttle arrives to make the first attempt at completing your objectives.
You may not ignore this rule because you forgot to disable antagonist rolling or because you're "not feeling like it." You must opt-in to play as an antagonist, so admins will operate on the assumption that you accept these rules in their entirety.
## Precedents - Your objectives [italics]may be ignored[/italics] if you feel that you have an idea or gimmick that will provide a more interesting round for all parties involved. This may only be done [bold]after you ask in admin help[/bold] and receive [bold]explicit[/bold] permission from a game admin to proceed with your idea. - If you think you are incapable of adding to the round as an antagonist, then you are encouraged to talk in admin help (F1) to find the best resolution for your situation.
# Teaming Up With Other Antagonists
Unless explicitly mentioned below, if your role is [color=red]Solo Antagonist[/color], you are not allowed to team up with other antagonists, [bold]including other antagonists like you[/bold] (e.g. [textlink="Heretics" link="Heretics"] cannot work together with other Heretics).
If you are a [bold]team[/bold] antagonist, you are expected to work with your team to complete your objectives. Otherwise, you should not team up with those who are not on your team.
If you believe the antagonist you're currently playing has a justification to team up with another potential antagonist in a scenario extraordinary to the examples below, [bold]always[/bold] ask in admin help beforehand.
- [textlink="Traitors" link="Traitors"] are [bold]always[/bold] allowed to team up with other Traitors regardless of their company alignment. Note that company alignment should be treated as flavor text, not as an exception to the teaming rules (except for [bold]Tiger Cooperative[/bold]). - Traitors that have the objective "Die a glorious death" may collaborate with [textlink="Nuclear Operatives" link="NuclearOperatives"]. The Nuclear Operatives do not have to help you, though they may treat you as an ally. - [textlink="SELF Agents" link="SELFAgent"] are [bold]always[/bold] allowed to team up with other SELF Agents. - [textlink="Internal Affairs Agents" link="NTAgent"] (IAAs) are [bold]always[/bold] allowed to team up with other IAAs or any complicit Central Command personnel. - [textlink="Changelings" link="Changelings"] are explicitly forbidden from working together. The only instance that allows a Changeling to work with an antagonist is if that individual is not a Changeling and is employed by the [bold]Tiger Cooperative[/bold]. - [textlink="Wizards" link="Wizard"] may only work with other members of the Space Wizards Federation. - [textlink="Space Ninjas" link="SpaceNinja"] may only work with those employed by the Spider Clan. - [textlink="Devils" link="Devil"] may assist any antagonist [bold]only[/bold] if their assistance directly results in, or is a clause of, a signed contract. - [textlink="Thieves" link="Thieves"] may cooperate with Traitors if their assistance aids with their objectives. This includes offering the [bold]Telecrystals[/bold] that may be acquired from their kit in exchange for Syndicate gear.
# Friendly Antagonism You may complete your objectives in such a way that minimizes suspicion or overall awareness of your actions. These actions must still be [italics]antagonistic[/italics] towards crew-aligned characters, and they must drive the round forward in a meaningful way. [bold]Explicitly acting friendly or supporting crew-aligned characters as an antagonist is forbidden.[/bold] If you have an idea that may fall under this ruling, you are required to ask in admin help beforehand to receive clearance from a game admin before you proceed.
As a Traitor, [textlink="Conspirator" link="Conspirators"], IAA, or SELF Agent, you have relaxed rules regarding friendly antagonism, as in-character you are still a crew member and may want to maintain your job. [bold]Once your objectives are completed,[/bold] you are free to act as any other member of the crew would.
## Precedents - You may support a crew-aligned individual or goal as long as your actions very clearly benefit you above all. An example of this would be assisting crew to defeat a station-ending threat to ensure that you are able to complete an objective requiring your own survival. - If you wish to [italics]blend in[/italics], you may assist crew-aligned individuals to maintain your cover or disguise. This should only be done in cases where inaction would result in immediate suspicion regarding your character’s motives. - As a [textlink="Space Dragon" link="MinorAntagonists"], though you're not obligated to, you may humor humanoids that happen to be recognized on your team as carp. - [textlink="Zombies" link="Zombies"] can (but are not obligated to) ignore IPCs, [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Silicons[/bold][/color], or other non-convertible humanoids until attacked first.
# Limitations on Round Impact or "Going Loud" Antagonists are expected to complete their objectives and, generally, to survive. This core idea should be reflected in the scope of your overall impact on the story of any given round. Any action taken that may fall outside this framework should have easily explainable roleplay motivation behind it.
Your interactions with crew-aligned individuals are especially important. An individual must have presented themself as a [bold]direct obstacle[/bold] towards any of your goals before they become valid (where you are entirely justified to immediately escalate to lethal force).
Being an "obstacle" can be either physical (e.g. following you outside of their department, attempting to handcuff or stun you, bolting doors, etc.) or verbal (e.g. calling [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] to your location, telling you to exit the area, threatening violence, etc.)
Antagonists are not expected to provide medical care or assistance in any way to crew-aligned individuals, but they should [bold]never seek to round remove someone[/bold] (i.e. make someone unrevivable) without having an objective to do so.
Any action that involves harming crew-aligned individuals or causing mass destruction outside of objective targets should have an easily demonstrable reasoning behind the action.
## Precedents - Making an active effort to kill a large number of otherwise uninvolved players while having the objective to escape alive and unrestrained. - Crippling or removing vital station infrastructure without an applicable objective. - Killing the entirety of the [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] department [italics]before[/italics] an officer has attempted to detain your character. - Killing nearby people because of what they "could" have done (e.g. shooting a nearby [color=#388c34][bold]Janitor[/bold][/color] because they "could have swung their mop.") Hypothetical scenarios are not a justification to act outside of this framework.
# Limitations on Mass Sabotage Any action taken that directly results in the sabotage of critical station infrastructure is limited to very few scenarios and very few antagonist objectives. The following list of antagonists should be treated as the [bold]ONLY[/bold] individuals that are allowed to perform mass station sabotage on [bold]ANY LEVEL[/bold]. - A Traitor that is assigned the "Die a glorious death" (DAGD) objective. It should be noted that having an objective to assist an individual with DAGD does not, by extension, give you the same freedoms that DAGD provides. - A Heretic that has ascended. - Nuclear Operatives if all operatives have agreed to this method. - Members of the Space Wizard Federation. - A [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Silicon[/bold][/color] with an applicable lawset. - [textlink="Blobs" link="Blob"], but [bold]not[/bold] their familiars (unless ordered by the Blob).
Any given antagonist not included on this list must assume that they have to prioritize their own survival before anything else. Any antagonist objective that requires that the individual remain alive for its completion disallows all forms of major station sabotage. Any action that causes mass harm or destruction may be subject to this ruling.
Additionally, you cannot repeatedly commit the same kind of mass sabotage. You're encouraged to [textlink="vary your gameplan," link="RuleGimmickCreativity"] but if it's not mass sabotage, you're allowed to use the same strategy if you want.
## Precedents - Loosing the Tesla or Singularity engine. - Using an EMAG on the station’s recycler. - Removal of the station’s SMES array. - Introducing [bold]any[/bold] gas into the station's atmospheric network that will directly impede the crew’s ability to perform their job (e.g. plasma, nitrous oxide, BZ). - The detonation or creation of a "maxcap" or canister bomb. - Crashing into the station with a shuttle or other spacefaring vehicle.
